overall_summary: Crypto faces clear headwinds today as hot inflation data locks in a December Fed hike, pushing yields and the dollar higher. Geopolitical shocks from the Middle East, tariffs, and Taiwan add risk-off pressure. Bitcoin-specific news is more constructive with support holding and a reserve bill advancing, but macro dominates the near-term tone.
key_points: Fed hike nearly certain after hot PCE data
Yields and dollar strengthen on hawkish outlook
Middle East strikes and tariff threats raise risk-off
Bitcoin holds June lows amid short liquidations
US Bitcoin reserve bill advances; Binance restored

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Hit Record $5.39B November Outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen $5.39 billion in net outflows so far in November, the largest monthly total on record and surpassing the prior June mark, with a seven-day streak draining over $3 billion led by BlackRock's IBIT. Bitcoin still rebounded above $61,000 amid broader risk-asset gains in tech futures and commodities after the Thanksgiving holiday. Traders should watch whether the selling pressure eases or continues to cap any recovery, especially with thin holiday liquidity.
items.impact: Persistent institutional outflows weigh on upside but extreme fear and bounce off lows leave room for relief rally

items.title: $7 Billion Bitcoin Options Expire Today
items.summary: Roughly $6.7 to $7 billion in Bitcoin options settle on Deribit today, about a quarter of open interest, with positioning now put-heavy around $60,000 to $75,000 strikes unlike the call-heavy October expiry. Arthur Hayes has flagged the risk of a weekend dump if the Fed stays hawkish into its blackout. With holiday-thin markets this could amplify volatility either way, so position sizing and gamma exposure matter for short-term traders.
items.impact: Expiry and thin liquidity raise odds of sharp two-way swings around current levels

items.title: US Bitcoin Reserve Bill Advances to House Floor
items.summary: The House Financial Services Committee has reported the American Reserve Modernization Act to the full House, placing it on the Union Calendar. The bill would codify a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and lock government-held BTC from sale, swap or pledge for at least 20 years after enactment. Passage remains uncertain with limited time left in the current Congress, but any progress reinforces long-term institutional legitimacy for Bitcoin.
items.impact: Positive regulatory signal that could support longer-term demand narrative if it advances further

items.title: Binance Fully Restores Withdrawals After $6.3B Hack
items.summary: Binance announced it has completed recovery work and fully lifted all withdrawal suspensions tied to the late-October $6.3 billion hack, the largest in crypto history, attributed to North Korea-linked actors. A few networks remain paused only for unrelated maintenance. Restoring full access removes a lingering confidence overhang for the largest exchange and should ease any residual liquidity concerns across the market.
items.impact: Removes major exchange operational risk and supports broader market stability

items.title: JPMorgan Flags Strategy mNAV Low as Capitulation Signal
items.summary: JPMorgan analysts say Strategy's mNAV multiple hit a record low of about 0.88 times the value of its Bitcoin holdings, below the prior June trough, calling it a clear capitulation signal for Bitcoin. The firm also noted intense ongoing outflows from BlackRock's IBIT even on brief price rebounds, and estimated miner production costs near $86,000. Capitulation readings like this often mark washed-out conditions that can precede relief moves, though miner stress remains a watchpoint.
items.impact: Classic capitulation marker that historically precedes stabilization or bounce after heavy selling

items.title: Bitcoin Defends June Low Support as Shorts Liquidate
items.summary: Glassnode notes Bitcoin continues to find buying support after retesting its June low, holding the daily close above that level while price reclaimed $61,000. The bounce has been fueled in part by short liquidations totaling tens of millions amid thin holiday trading and a broader rebound in Nasdaq futures, gold and silver. Traders care because a confirmed hold of this multi-month support turns the technical picture more constructive after the sharp November drawdown.
items.impact: Confirmed support hold plus short squeeze can extend the relief rally if volume confirms

items.title: Hot Core PCE and GDP Revision Lock In December Fed Hike
items.summary: October core PCE rose to 3.3 percent year-over-year, beating forecasts and hitting a multi-year high, while headline PCE hit 3.8 percent. At the same time third-quarter GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3 percent annualized. Traders should care because this combination of sticky inflation and strong growth has markets pricing a near-certain 25 basis point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting, tightening financial conditions further.
items.impact: Higher rates and stronger dollar pressure risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Beige Book Confirms Sticky Inflation and Moderate Growth
items.summary: The latest Federal Reserve Beige Book showed economic activity expanding at a slight to moderate pace in most districts, with employment rising and prices continuing to increase moderately. Contacts cited ongoing cost pressures from energy, tariffs, and other inputs that businesses struggle to fully pass on. This qualitative survey reinforces the case for further tightening just two weeks before the next rate decision.
items.impact: Supports hawkish Fed stance and elevated rate path

items.title: Treasury Yields Climb as Markets Reopen After Holiday
items.summary: US Treasury yields rose in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session, with the 10-year yield climbing around 7 basis points toward 4.92 percent and the 2-year also higher. The move comes after this week's strong growth and inflation data locked in December hike expectations. Bond traders are watching the upcoming Fed blackout and December meeting for the next major catalyst.
items.impact: Rising yields tighten financial conditions and weigh on equities and crypto

items.title: US Dollar Holds Near Multi-Month Highs on Hawkish Fed
items.summary: The dollar index hovered near 103.7 to 104, close to recent 20-plus month peaks, supported by resilient US data and firm rate-hike odds even as risk sentiment improved slightly. Safe-haven flows and yield differentials continue to underpin the greenback in thin holiday trading. A strong dollar typically acts as a headwind for commodities and risk assets globally.
items.impact: Strong DXY pressures Bitcoin and other risk assets

items.title: Jobless Claims Stay Low, Signaling Resilient Labor Market
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell more than expected to 189,000 for the week ending November 21, with continuing claims also dropping sharply. The data, released early ahead of Thanksgiving, points to a still-tight labor market with limited layoffs. Strong employment keeps wage and demand pressures alive, giving the Fed little reason to pause its tightening path.
items.impact: Firm labor data supports higher-for-longer rates

items.title: Markets Price Near-Certain December Rate Hike Amid Blackout
items.summary: Futures now assign roughly 95 to 99 percent odds of a 25 basis point Fed hike on December 9, lifting the target range to 4.00-4.25 percent, with further tightening possible early next year. The Fed communications blackout begins soon, leaving little new guidance before the meeting. Traders must position around the high probability of tighter policy even as equity volatility from AI concerns lingers.
items.impact: Elevated rate expectations keep pressure on liquidity-sensitive assets

items.title: Houthi Strike Hits Saudi Jazan Refinery; Hormuz Mines Claimed
items.summary: A projectile blamed on Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, killing a worker, injuring others and temporarily halting some operations. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately claimed two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices jumped, with Brent near multi-week highs on fresh supply fears from the Gulf. Traders should watch this closely because sustained Middle East energy disruption lifts inflation risks and can spark risk-off moves across equities and crypto.
items.impact: Higher oil and energy volatility pressure risk assets

items.title: Iran-Blamed Drone Attack in Kuwait Kills Two Italians
items.summary: Kuwait said Iranian drones hit a vital facility, killing two Italian technicians from Rheinmetall working on air defenses and injuring others. Italy confirmed the deaths; Iran denied any involvement, called the incident suspicious and offered a joint probe. This marks a notable widening of the Iran-related conflict into another Gulf state with European casualties. Crypto traders care because fresh escalation raises black-swan geopolitical risk and safe-haven flows that can hit Bitcoin short-term.
items.impact: Heightened Middle East war risk fuels risk-off sentiment

items.title: Trump Proposes New Tariffs on China and 13 Others
items.summary: The US unveiled proposed Section 301 tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners over alleged excess industrial capacity, with China facing 20 percent that could rise to 40 percent. China, the EU, Japan and others rejected the premise and warned of countermeasures while noting existing deal caps. The duties face comment periods and could bite in early 2027. This matters for markets because renewed trade war uncertainty hits global growth expectations and risk appetite, including crypto.
items.impact: Trade-war escalation weighs on global risk assets

items.title: Trump Urges Putin Pullback as Russia Strikes Ukraine Hard
items.summary: President Trump said he pressed Putin to pull back all military aggression across Europe during recent China talks, hoping for a quick Ukraine deal, after meeting NATO's Rutte. Overnight Russian ballistic missiles and over 100 drones hit Kyiv and other cities; Zelensky warned of another major power-grid strike. Ukraine reported hits on Russian energy and airfield targets. The mix of diplomatic messaging and battlefield escalation keeps uncertainty high for risk assets.
items.impact: Diplomacy hope offset by ongoing war escalation

items.title: China Flies 30 Warplanes Near Taiwan Ahead of Elections
items.summary: On the final campaign day before Taiwan's local elections, Taipei reported 30 Chinese military aircraft, 26 crossing the median line, in a joint combat readiness patrol with warships. Beijing continues pressure tactics while the vote itself centers more on domestic issues. Results come Saturday. Traders watch Taiwan Strait tension because any spike threatens semiconductor supply chains and broader Asia risk sentiment that feeds into crypto.
items.impact: Elevated Taiwan Strait risk hits Asia and tech sentiment

items.title: EU Summit Deadlocks on Budget and Ukraine Loan
items.summary: European leaders ended a special summit without agreement on the long-term budget or a 45-billion-euro loan for Ukraine in 2027, deferring talks to mid-December. Several central and eastern states objected to using EU funds for military aid. Public support for Ukraine aid is softening in key countries like Germany. Delayed European backing adds another layer of uncertainty to the Ukraine conflict and eurozone cohesion that markets price into risk assets.
items.impact: Ukraine funding delay adds mild political uncertainty
